title: Introduce credential lease + adaptive retry optimizer; align config names with TS/Go
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Intermittent streaming interruptions in long-lived streams were traced to tightly-coupled token refresh windows and aggressive client-side retry gates. Teams asked for an ergonomic primitive that: 1) makes token lifetime management explicit to SDK consumers, 2) lets SDKs pre-emptively acquire/renew short-lived leases used for streaming sessions, and 3) tunes retry windows automatically based on lease health and observed stream heartbeat.

This PR introduces a lightweight 'CredentialLease' primitive in the Python SDK, an adaptive retry optimizer that consults lease health to scale retry backoff ceilings, and harmonizes top-level config key names with companion PRs in the TypeScript and Go SDKs (see linked PRs). The change is intended to be opt-in: defaults preserve current behaviour.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add credentials/lease.py: CredentialLease, LeaseManager, TTL jittering, prefetch policy, and metrics hooks.
- Add retry/optimizer.py: AdaptiveRetryOptimizer which adjusts retry windows based on lease state and streaming heartbeat.
- API ergonomics: expose 'lease' argument on StreamingClient and add convenience 'with_lease' context manager.
- Cross-SDK parity: rename config keys to `lease_ttl`, `lease_prefetch_margin`, and `retry_ceiling_ms` to match TS/Go (backwards-compatible aliases preserved).
- Tests: unit tests for lease lifecycle, integration mock for streaming with simulated token rotation, and e2e smoke for retry elasticity.
- Docs: updated SDK reference and quickstart snippet demonstrating a streaming consumer using a CredentialLease.
- Changelog and version bump to 1.29.0.dev -> will be released as 1.29.0.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration smoke verified locally against staging token service
- [x] Docs snippets updated
- [x] Config rename documented and backward aliases included
- [x] Lint and type checks green

Compatibility notes: The change is backwards compatible by default; consumers who want the new behavior must pass `lease=CredentialLease(...)` when constructing StreamingClient or set the new config keys. We preserved old config names via deprecation warnings for one release cycle.

review_comments:
Diego: asked for clearer defaults and suggested default lease_ttl=120s instead of 60s; caught a race in LeaseManager.shutdown that could double-free a timer.
Marta: requested docs example that shows safe migration from old config keys; asked to add a deprecation warning when old keys are used.
Oliver: requested a small perf test to ensure the locker used by LeaseManager doesn't add contention under 2500 concurrent streams.
Author response: Increased default lease_ttl to 120s, added jitter and exponential reclaim backoff, added deprecation shim for old config names, replaced coarse lock with a per-lease atomic flag to reduce contention, and added a lightweight concurrency test (2500 simulated streams) to integration harness. Reviewers approved after last changes.

merge_result: Merged via squash on 2026-02-20. Merge commit: squash -> 3 logical changes bundled. Merge notes: opted to keep deprecation warnings for one release cycle and publish migration guide in docs. Coordinated merges in TS/Go SDK repos scheduled and linked from the release notes.
release_notes:
- Introduce CredentialLease primitive for optional streaming token prefetch/renew.
- Add AdaptiveRetryOptimizer to improve retry behaviour for long-lived streaming sessions.
- Align SDK config names across Python/TypeScript/Go: lease_ttl, lease_prefetch_margin, retry_ceiling_ms (old names still supported with deprecation warnings).
- Minor version bump planned to 1.29.0.
- No breaking changes by default; opt-in feature.
notes: Companion PRs: typescript#23412, go#981726 (coordinate for simultaneous release). Runtime observation: reduced sustained transient reconnects in staging when lease prefetch enabled. Follow-up items: telemetry to surface lease refresh failures, dashboard widget showing lease health across streams.
